Create an HTML report for a region of the genome

Source: R/report.R
render_report.Rd

Produces a handout-style HTML report for a gene or region: a summary of the data, PCA, admixture, Fst, heterozygosity, allele frequencies of key SNPs (with maps) and LD, plus a methods section recording exactly how the results were produced. The report is a single self-contained HTML file that can be emailed, uploaded to a virtual learning environment, or printed.

Usage

render_report(
  x,
  pop = NULL,
  super_pop = NULL,
  focal_snps = NULL,
  k = 2:5,
  reps = 5,
  min_maf = 0.01,
  seed = 1,
  version = c("staff", "student"),
  title = NULL,
  output_dir = ".",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

What to report on. Either a character vector of gene symbols or coordinates (one report is made for each; see fetch_region()), or a snpscape object you have prepared yourself (e.g. combining several regions).

pop, super_pop

Populations or super-populations to include (see keep_pops()). NULL includes everyone.

focal_snps

rs numbers or SNP IDs to show allele frequencies for.

k

The numbers of ancestral groups for admixture analysis.

reps

Number of admixture runs for each K.

min_maf

Minimum minor allele frequency for SNPs (see filter_snps()).

seed

Random seed, so that the same settings always give the same report.

version

"staff" (with notes for staff) or "student" (without).

title

Report title. By default, made from the region name.

output_dir

Folder to save reports in. Created if needed.

verbose

Print progress messages.

Value

The paths of the created HTML files, invisibly.

Details

Staff and student versions

The staff version (the default) adds a "Notes for staff" section with the expected pattern and its explanation, for genes in teaching_genes. The student version leaves this out, so students can interpret the results themselves.

Which data are used for what

The report applies filter_snps() itself, using min_maf:

  • PCA and admixture use LD-pruned SNPs, because these methods assume SNPs are independent.

  • Allele frequencies, Fst and heterozygosity use all SNPs that pass the frequency filter.

  • LD heatmaps use SNPs with a minor allele frequency of at least 5%, one heatmap per super-population, without pruning.

Key SNPs

The allele frequency section shows the SNPs given in focal_snps. If none are given, it uses the SNPs listed for the gene in teaching_snps, or, for other regions, the SNP whose frequency differs most between super-populations.

Requirements and run time

Reports are made with Quarto, which is installed together with RStudio (or from https://quarto.org). Making a report takes from under a minute to a few minutes, mostly for the admixture analysis; use fewer k values or reps to speed it up.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
render_report("LCT")

# one report per gene, for a chosen set of populations
render_report(
  c("LCT", "SLC24A5", "ACKR1"),
  pop = c("YRI", "LWK", "GBR", "FIN", "CHB", "JPT", "GIH", "PEL"),
  output_dir = "handouts"
)

# student version, for a region with no well-known genes
render_report("chr18:1000000-1500000", version = "student")
} # }
